edges.description: Loss of one functional CDC42BPB allele is expected to reduce MRCKbeta kinase activity toward the myosin II regulatory light chain. This step is inferred from the variant class and the kinase's normal function; it has not been measured in patient cells.
CDC42BPB variants are associated with structural brain anomalies in the founding series. The intervening cellular steps are not established.

In cultured neurons, MRCKbeta phosphorylation of the myosin regulatory light chain drives the actin rearrangement needed for dendrite outgrowth and spine formation. Whether reduced MRCKbeta produces a dendritic defect in patients is not known.
Hypothesized. Defective dendrite development would contribute to disturbed brain development, but no study has examined neurons or brain tissue carrying a CDC42BPB variant.
Associative. Developmental delay occurs with and without a structural anomaly, so the specific brain abnormality producing it is not known.
Associative. The neural basis of the intellectual disability is not established.
Associative. The neural basis of autism in this disorder is not established.
Associative. Hypotonia is attributed to the central nervous system involvement; no peripheral or muscle cause has been reported.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline CDC42BPB variant, usually arising de novo. Frameshift and nonsense variants are predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay and cause haploinsufficiency. Missense variants cluster in the kinase domain, the citron homology domain, and a 20-amino-acid segment between two coiled-coil regions; whether they reduce kinase function or act otherwise has not been tested.

nodes.description: A proposed cellular consequence of reduced MRCKbeta: defective actin-dependent dendrite outgrowth and spine formation in developing neurons. Supported only by normal-function studies of MRCKbeta; no patient neurons or CDC42BPB-variant neuronal models have been examined.

evidence.snippet: MRCKβ FL or MRCKβ 1 to 430, but not MRCKβ K105M, was able to rescue Dasm1 knockdown-induced decrease of total dendrite length (left panel) and dendritic branch numbers (right panel) in hippocampal neurons.

nodes.description: MRCKbeta is a CDC42-activated AGC-family kinase that phosphorylates the myosin II regulatory light chain and so controls actomyosin contractility and actin rearrangement. Reduced MRCKbeta dosage is expected to weaken this regulation. The node describes the kinase's established normal function; its reduction in patients is inferred.
